title: Mutable object bound as a default argument value
purpose: Prevent the classic shared-mutable-default bug an authoring LLM reproduces from corpora: the default object is created once and mutated residual across calls.
trigger: A function parameter's default value is a list/dict/set literal (or a fresh-mutable constructor call such as list(), dict(), set()) producing an object that carries in-place mutation semantics.
correct: Bind None as the default and construct a fresh mutable inside the body only when the argument is None; keep all per-call state local to that call.
compiler_relationship: Statistically safe and almost always intended-wrong; a deliberate shared-cache default is rare and should be an explicit documented decision, not a bare literal.
return_semantics: A LanguageRulePage may be opened and then returned to the originating cycle.
